interactions.note: The epitope of M18 scFv on PA domain 4 (PAD4) was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. There are four molecules in the crystallographic asymmetric unit. PDB chains for each complex are: Complex I : Antibody heavy-chain: F, Antibody light-chain: F, epitope chain: J. Complex II : Antibody heavy-chain: G, Antibody light-chain: G, epitope chain: K. Complex III : Antibody heavy-chain: H, Antibody light-chain: H, epitope chain: L. Complex IV : Antibody heavy-chain: I, Antibody light-chain: I, epitope chain: M. In each complex the heavy and light chains have the same PDB chain letter because they are linked together. There was no electron density for the 20 amino acids linking the C-terminus of the light chain to the N-terminus of the heavy chain of the M18 scFv.  Each complex is related to a second complex by a non-crystallographic 2-fold rotation with the dimer interface of this greater dimer involving principally β-strands of the light chain 62-67 and 70-74. The two greater dimer particles in the asymmetric unit are, in turn, related by a rotation of 178 degrees. Contact between the greater dimer particles of the asymmetric unit involves a single PAD4 monomer in each. In two of the antibody molecules, residues 1-113 of the heavy chain are observed while in the other two, the first heavy chain residue cannot be seen. Also, for three of the PAD4 molecules, electron density for residues 592-735 is observed, but in the fourth, only residues 593-735 are seen. The four complexes are essentially identical, with the largest differences seen in the N-terminal loop of PAD4, residues 592-605.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.8 angstroms
